brief: SG's postmortem argues the September FOMC hike signals inflation concern has broadened beyond energy: the statement dropped its supply-shock framing for inflation and pledged a timelier return to 2%, with no dissents on the 25bp move to 3.75%-4%. The SEP reinforced this: GDP revised up, unemployment revised down to 4.1% (below the Fed's 4.2% long-run estimate), and core PCE for 2026 revised up to 3.4%. Most members see upside inflation risk and none see downside employment risk, which SG reads as the Committee perceiving lower stagflation risk and therefore focusing squarely on inflation. The 2026 median dot now implies 50bp of hikes this year (12 of 19 aligned), while 2027 dots split four cutters versus eight hikers, and the long-run dot rose to 3.2%. Chair Warsh called current policy not restrictive and framed the hike as removing accommodation. SG keeps its call for two more 25bp hikes in December and March (75bp total), expecting the Committee to converge on unwinding the 2025 insurance cuts but not go further restrictive for now, a view conditional on inflation data not disappointing.
